_meta.source: Archetype names, descriptions and segment mappings come from Banfield Design Co.'s written client-type document. Fields marked in 'draft_fields' are inferred from that document and the Oct 2 / Oct 9 meeting transcripts and must be reviewed by Banfield before use.
_meta.visibility: Team-facing only. Never show archetype ids, labels or scores to the client.
_meta.scoring: Answer options in the question bank carry weights keyed by archetype id. Sum weights, normalize to percentages and report the blend (e.g. 60% analytical_validator / 30% hands_on_controller). Scoring must keep working if archetypes are added or removed.

archetypes.label: The Decisive Delegator
archetypes.description: Busy professional lives; want the design team to take ownership. Prefer two excellent options to ten possibilities and may lose patience with unnecessary meetings.
signals: Prefers a clear recommendation from someone experienced
Wants the design team to take the lead
Open to a concept different from what they pictured
Completes the quiz quickly; short open-text answers
archetypes.communication: Short, decisive emails with a clear recommendation and next step. Bullet points, not essays.
archetypes.pacing: Fewer, tightly agendaed meetings. Present two strong options, not a range.
archetypes.pitch: Full-service package where Banfield owns the process end to end.
risks: May approve quickly and want to revisit later if not briefed on consequences
archetypes.brief_tips: Lead with the outcome and timeline. Respect their time from the first call.

archetypes.label: The Analytical Validator
archetypes.description: Appreciates specifications, comparative pricing, energy performance and documented reasoning. May challenge a recommendation not because they distrust the designer, but because they want to understand it.
signals: Researches thoroughly before feeling confident
Wants to understand the reasoning before deciding
Values a clear understanding of costs
Long, detailed open-text answers; high self-rated detail orientation
archetypes.communication: Detailed written follow-ups with specs, comparisons and the reasoning behind each recommendation.
archetypes.pacing: Allow time between decisions for review. Send materials ahead of meetings.
archetypes.pitch: Structured process with documented decision points; highlight performance and energy expertise.
risks: Questions can be misread as distrust
Decisions slow down without supporting evidence
archetypes.brief_tips: Bring the data. Treat challenges as engagement, not pushback.

archetypes.label: The Cautious Reassurance Seeker
archetypes.tagline: Risk-sensitive. Thoughtful. Needs confidence and validation.
archetypes.description: Often making one of the largest discretionary investments of their lives and can find design decisions intimidating. May fear costly mistakes, unfamiliar terminology or unexpected expenses. Looks to approval from others (builders/trades, family and friends).
signals: Likes discussing decisions with the people involved
Not sure how involved to be; wants to learn how the process works
Prefers to stay close to what they originally imagined
Values knowing what happens next and frequent progress updates
Mentions past bad experiences or nervousness about cost
archetypes.communication: Warm, plain-language updates with no jargon. Explain what happens next and why.
archetypes.pacing: Smaller decisions spread out; check in often. Avoid presenting too many possibilities at once.
archetypes.pitch: Guided process with clear milestones, cost transparency and predictable check-ins.
risks: Third-party opinions (trades, family) can override decisions
Needs trust built before letting go of their own plan
archetypes.brief_tips: Build trust before design. Name the next step at the end of every interaction.

archetypes.label: The Creative Collaborator
archetypes.description: Enjoys design, collects inspiration and wants to participate. May come with extensive Pinterest boards and a strong sense of personal style. Higher chance of scope creep as they become inspired.
signals: Prefers to explore ideas and see where they lead
Enjoys collaborating at design milestones
Excited to explore a new perspective
Values seeing visualizations before committing
Uploads inspiration images; rich answers to style and mood questions
archetypes.communication: Visual-first: mood boards, renderings, images over text.
archetypes.pacing: Build in collaborative working sessions at key milestones.
archetypes.pitch: Collaborative design process with visualization; set scope boundaries early.
risks: Scope creep as new ideas emerge
Strong personal style can conflict with team recommendations
archetypes.brief_tips: Invite their ideas, then anchor every addition back to scope and budget.

archetypes.label: The Hands-On Controller
archetypes.description: Prefers to maintain visibility into budgets, decisions, vendors and timelines. May have managed major projects professionally and expects significant involvement.
signals: Wants to be closely involved in selections and decisions
Wants to compare a new concept with their original vision
Values being involved in the details and understanding why choices are made
Values a clear understanding of costs and where the budget is going
archetypes.communication: Regular structured status updates covering budget, timeline, vendors and open decisions.
archetypes.pacing: Agree on decision checkpoints up front; keep them visible.
archetypes.pitch: Hourly or phased engagement with transparent tracking; position Banfield as a strategic teammate.
risks: Friction if they feel excluded from vendor or budget decisions
May second-guess trades or the design team
archetypes.brief_tips: Share the plan and the numbers early. Give them clear lanes for involvement.
